- **Bishop Theorem 4.2's final step is not merely unproved — it is false as stated.** The proof bounds the interior of a rectangle by boundary values of `|f − f(0) − L|` using the maximum principle for open maps, but `f − L` is not open. Counterexample: `f(z) = z + z|z|(1−|z|)` on the closed unit disc is a homeomorphism with `Df(0) = id`, and `|f − id| = |z|²(1−|z|)` has supremum `4/27` at `|z| = 2/3` while vanishing on `|z| = 1`.
- **The exact classical input** is the Gehring–Lehto total-differentiability theorem (with `J_f ≥ 0` a.e. for sense-preserving ACL homeomorphisms). A complete modern authority is located — Lehto–Virtanen, *Quasiconformal Mappings in the Plane*, 2nd ed., pp. 10 and 128–130 (via Ryazanov–Srebro–Yakubov 2007, Prop. 3.27) — but not available to read here, so no proof is claimed.
- I recorded a complete reduction for the owner: with that one theorem supplied (local transcript or the same exact-citation exception the owner granted elsewhere in this run), the elementary winding-number/Vitali arguments close item 10 steps 1.1/3.1, item 12(iii)'s differentiability interface, item 13's null-set transfer, and item 14 steps 1.2–1.4 — i.e. all twelve escalations reduce to this single input plus the batch-14 supplier.
